dedupe_keys.name: zaragoza water saving city programme climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Zaragoza Water Saving City programme, started in 1996 after water shortages, which combined awareness campaigns, examples of good practice, voluntary commitments by citizens and businesses and revised tariffs under a municipal Water Commission. The 1996-2010 strategic plan aimed to cut city consumption from 84.7 million m3 in 1995 to 65 million m3 by 2010, and the page reports a reduction of nearly 30 per cent; a second Water Management and Quality Improvement Plan followed in 2010. Coverage is the city of Zaragoza in Spain. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2020 and updated in 2026. Caveats: no full cost evaluation is public, and economic constraints slowed further progress. Simulation uses: demand reduction scenarios for urban water supply planning under drought. Related records: the Dunkerque eco-social tariff case study (case_study-dunkerque-eco-social-water-tariff).
